questions.q: Data engineers, analysts and ML engineers must share governed data. Consumers should request access to published datasets, owners approve, and access is granted through Lake Formation. Which approach fits?

options.t: Separate SageMaker Studio domains with shared S3 bucket policies
options.why: Wrong: no publish, subscribe and approve workflow, and bucket policies bypass Lake Formation governance.

options.t: SageMaker Unified Studio projects with SageMaker Catalog subscriptions
options.why: Right: Catalog (built on DataZone) lets owners publish assets and approve subscriptions, granted through Lake Formation.

options.t: SageMaker Feature Store with cross-account sharing
options.why: Wrong: Feature Store serves ML features, it is not a business data catalog with approval workflows.
Wrong: the Registry versions models, not data assets.

questions.explain: Publish, subscribe, approve, grant via Lake Formation is SageMaker Catalog in Unified Studio.
questions.remember: Governed data sharing with request/approve across teams → SageMaker Unified Studio projects plus SageMaker Catalog subscriptions (DataZone, Lake Formation grants).
variants: Only ML teams need a hub for pretrained models → JumpStart.
A project user cannot read data → check the project role's Lake Formation/S3 permissions or whether the subscription was approved.
A business glossary and metadata forms are needed → SageMaker Catalog.

questions.q: A large company wants each business unit to govern its own projects and set its own owners inside a single SageMaker Unified Studio domain. Which construct delegates this governance?

options.why: Right: domain units form a hierarchy in the domain, with their own owners, project creation rights and shared rules.
Wrong: profiles choose which capabilities (blueprints) a new project gets, not who governs.
Wrong: a space is a workspace for an app, not a governance boundary.
Wrong: blueprints deploy resources such as Glue or EMR through CloudFormation.

questions.explain: Domain units delegate governance inside a Unified Studio domain.
questions.remember: Delegate governance per business unit in Unified Studio → domain units; the collaboration unit with its role, S3 location and members is the project.
variants: Choose which capabilities a new project gets (SQL analytics, ML and GenAI) → project profiles.
The unit that holds the project role, S3 location and compute connections → project.
Each Studio person has a profile in a classic Studio domain → user profile.

questions.q: Security requires that no SageMaker Studio notebook traffic crosses the public internet. Which domain setting meets this?

options.why: Wrong: this is the default and uses SageMaker-managed internet access.

options.t: A shared space for all users
options.why: Wrong: a shared space is about co-editing, not network paths.
Wrong: idle shutdown saves cost, it does not change network paths.

options.t: VpcOnly network access type with VPC endpoints or NAT
options.why: Right: all traffic goes through your VPC, and you provide endpoints (SageMaker API/runtime, S3, STS, Logs, ECR) or NAT.

questions.explain: VpcOnly routes everything through your VPC.
questions.remember: No internet for Studio → VpcOnly domain, plus VPC endpoints for SageMaker API/runtime, S3, STS, CloudWatch Logs and ECR.
variants: A VpcOnly app is stuck starting → missing endpoints or the security group lacks NFS (2049) to EFS.
Notebooks in VpcOnly need to install packages → NAT gateway or mirrors such as CodeArtifact.
Enforce VPC attachment for jobs → condition key sagemaker:VpcSubnets.

questions.q: Analysts want to clean data visually, with a natural-language option, and export the repeatable flow as a SageMaker Pipelines step. Which tool fits?

options.why: Wrong: it builds labeled datasets with human workforces.
Wrong: it monitors endpoints in production, not data prep.
Right: visual and natural-language prep with built-in transforms, exportable to Pipelines, S3 or Feature Store.
Wrong: it inspects training tensors and system metrics.

questions.explain: Data Wrangler (now in Canvas) is the visual prep tool with export to Pipelines.
questions.remember: Visual or no-code data prep for ML with repeatable exportable flows → Data Wrangler in Canvas; heavy production ETL → Glue or EMR.
variants: Visual prep for analytics rather than ML → Glue DataBrew.
Large Spark transforms without a cluster to manage → SageMaker Processing.
Large nightly ETL → Glue or EMR, cheaper and simpler.

questions.q: Auditors ask which datasets, code and training job produced a model in production. Which SageMaker capability records these relationships automatically for Pipelines executions?

options.why: Right: it records artifacts, actions, contexts and associations, and is auto-created for Pipelines executions.
Wrong: it gives one view of models and monitoring status, not the full artifact graph.
Wrong: it logs requests and responses, not how the model was built.
Wrong: they show who called APIs, not data-to-model relationships.

questions.explain: ML Lineage Tracking links data, code and model.
questions.remember: Which data and job produced this model → ML Lineage Tracking (with Pipelines executions, Registry versions and MLflow runs).
variants: Lineage on the data side → SageMaker Catalog (DataZone) lineage, Glue Data Catalog and Lake Formation.
Documentation of intended use and risks → Model Cards.
Who invoked an endpoint → CloudTrail data events for InvokeEndpoint.

questions.q: A fraud model needs the same customer features in training and in real-time inference, with the latest values read in a few milliseconds and full history kept for training. What should the team use?

options.why: Wrong: it can serve features but has no feature versioning, offline join tooling or catalog.

options.t: Feature Store with online and offline stores
options.why: Right: the online store returns the latest record per ID quickly and the offline store keeps append-only history in S3 for training.

options.t: An S3 bucket of CSV files read by the endpoint
options.why: Wrong: too slow for millisecond reads and no point-in-time history.

options.t: Feature Store with only the online store
options.why: Wrong: it keeps only the latest record, so history for training is lost.

questions.explain: Online for fresh serving, offline for training history.
questions.remember: Same features in training and serving, low-millisecond reads → Feature Store with both stores; online keeps only the latest record, offline is append-only history queried with Athena.
variants: Only batch training needs history → offline store only.
A newer record returns old data → its event time is older than the stored record, so it was ignored.
Pure analytics with no serving → skip Feature Store.

questions.q: A team trains on a few hundred GB of data and wants training to start quickly without downloading everything to the instance volume first. Which option fits?

options.why: Wrong: it downloads the entire dataset to EBS before training starts.
Wrong: it splits objects across instances but does not change the download behaviour.
Wrong: more disk does not remove the download wait.

options.t: FastFile mode or Pipe mode, or FSx for Lustre
options.why: Right: they stream data on demand, so training starts fast.

questions.explain: Streaming input modes avoid the full download.
questions.remember: Large dataset and fast training start → FastFile (local-filesystem view) or Pipe (sequential stream) mode, or FSx for Lustre for repeated epochs.
variants: Many small S3 files slow training → shard or combine files.
Repeated experiments waste startup time → managed warm pools (billed while warm).
Small dataset, simplest setup → File mode.

questions.q: A company must score 200 million rows every night. No endpoint is needed outside the batch window, and cost must stay low. Which design fits?

options.why: Wrong: instance-hours are billed even when idle, and it is not built for whole datasets.
Wrong: it targets small models with spiky traffic, not bulk scoring.

options.t: Batch Transform over many split input files with several instances
options.why: Right: no persistent endpoint, and parallelism comes from mapping S3 objects to instances.

options.t: An asynchronous endpoint with one large input file
options.why: Wrong: async is for large single payloads with queueing, and one big file would not spread across instances.

questions.explain: Batch Transform is offline scoring with no persistent endpoint.
questions.remember: Score a whole dataset offline → Batch Transform; split the input into many files, because one big file uses only one instance.
variants: One 500 MB image per request, results can wait → asynchronous inference (up to 1 GB, 1 hour).
Steady low-latency traffic → real-time endpoint with autoscaling across 2 or more AZs.
Spiky traffic, small CPU model, cold start acceptable → serverless inference.

questions.q: A data scientist needs inference on a GPU inside a VPC with data capture enabled. Traffic is unpredictable and the team wants to scale to zero. What is the best fit?

options.why: Wrong: it does not support GPUs, VPC config or data capture.

options.t: A real-time endpoint with autoscaling and a schedule to scale down
options.why: Right: real-time supports GPU, VPC and data capture, and the scheduled scale-down limits idle instance-hours.
Wrong: it is offline and has no live endpoint to invoke.
Wrong: multi-model endpoints are not supported on serverless.

questions.explain: Serverless lacks GPU, VPC and data capture, so use real-time.
questions.remember: Need GPU, VPC, data capture, multiple variants or Model Monitor → real-time endpoint; serverless supports none of them.
variants: Large payload up to 1 GB and scale to zero → asynchronous inference.
Serverless cold starts hurt a predictable burst → provisioned concurrency, capped at max concurrency.
Many small sparse-traffic models → multi-model endpoint on real-time.

questions.q: A new ML project needs drift monitoring. The team tries to set up SageMaker Model Monitor but the account cannot. What is the AWS-recommended path?

options.t: Keep requesting Model Monitor through Service Quotas
options.why: Wrong: Model Monitor is closed to new customers, which is not a quota issue.

options.t: Use Ground Truth to label drift
options.why: Wrong: Ground Truth builds labeled datasets and is also closed to new customers.

options.t: Use Debugger rules on the endpoint
options.why: Wrong: Debugger watches training jobs and is in maintenance mode.

options.t: Open-source monitoring with MLflow and Evidently, EventBridge, SNS and CloudWatch or QuickSight
options.why: Right: this is the AWS-suggested replacement, with data capture feeding scheduled drift checks.

questions.explain: Model Monitor no longer accepts new customers.
questions.remember: Model Monitor and Clarify are closed to new customers (from 30 July 2026) → MLflow plus Evidently for drift, SHAP and fmeval for explanations, CloudWatch alarms for alerts.
variants: Bias and explainability needed for a new project → pandas/scikit-learn bias metrics and SHAP, logged to MLflow.
Drift alarm should trigger retraining → EventBridge starts a Pipelines execution.
Labels arrive days later → join by inference ID and compute quality metrics on a schedule.
